title: WPPIL/170/2015 of Sarop Singh Pundir Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (PIL) No.170 of 2015

Sarop Singh Pundir .......Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ......Respondents
Mr. Gopal K. Verma, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, Deputy Advocate General for the State/respondent nos.1 to 3.
Mr. Ravi Babulkar, Advocate for respondent no.4.
Mr. Anurag Bisaria, Advocate for respondent nos.5 & 6.
Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Standing Counsel for Union of India/respondent no.7.
Dated: 09.10.2015
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)

Petitioner challenges Government Order dated
06.05.2015 (Annexure-3). He also seeks a direction to respondent
nos.4 not to construct trenching ground on the bank of holy river
Ganga, on the land belonging to Gram Samaj of Village Khadri
Kharak Maf Tehsil Rishikesh, District Dehradun.
2. Briefly put, the case of the petitioner is as follows:

By the impugned order, the State Government has made
over 10 acres of land of the 4th respondent for construction of the
trenching ground. It is contended, inter alia, that this site is actually
located very near to holy river Ganga and he seeks to substantiate it
with certain photographs.
3. Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the 4th
respondent would submit that search for site for trenching ground

began in 2009 and the Government has allotted the land and the land
has been got mutated in the name of the 4th respondent. That is all that
has happened. According to him, further various procedures will have
to be undergone before the land is used as a trenching ground. They
have to get various permission under various laws. According to him,
in short, this petition is premature.
4. We would think that at this juncture, we need not
consider the issue raised by the petitioner. We record the stand of the
4th respondent that all that has happened is that the land (10 acres) has
been got mutated in his name. It will have to take steps for
establishing it as a trenching ground since various procedures in law
would have to be undergone. We leave it open to the petitioner to
raise all his contentions before the statutory Authorities. We further
leave open to the petitioner if he is ultimately aggrieved to seek the
same reliefs, which he has sought in the writ petition by filling a fresh
writ petition. Leaving open the contention of the petitioner, the writ
petition is dismissed.
 (V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 09.10.2015 09.10.2015
